question: QA1: for the MVP, does a modular monolith with hard internal contracts provide a better safety, determinism and operability boundary than splitting the runtime into containers?

options.modular_monolith: One process; gateway/journal/engine/workers as modules behind hard internal contracts; one SQLite/WAL store; in-process calls.
options.container_split: Separate processes/containers for gateway, engine, workers and audit store; RPC between them; possibly more than one host.

scoring: Integer 1..5 per option per dimension; 5 is best for MVP safety, determinism and operability; evidence arrays cite bundle source ids; totals are unweighted sums; hard invariants gate before totals.

baseline.note: Single-process, single-host SQLite/WAL benchmark (seed 20260824); explicitly excludes multi-process/multi-host and production SLOs.

modular_monolith.notes: The in-process gateway is the only effects path; policy state is read from the one authoritative store; no cross-process copies exist.

container_split.notes: The gateway becomes a network service and other containers are tempted to cache policy/capability state; a duplicated policy cache is a standing invariant-5..7 risk and creates an unreviewed trust boundary.

modular_monolith.notes: Transition + hash-chained audit event + anchor head update commit in one SQLite transaction; rollback leaves state and audit consistent by construction.

container_split.notes: Splitting transition and audit across processes/streams risks partial audit on crash, chain forks and anchor divergence; preserving invariant 8 would need a distributed transaction the MVP does not have.

modular_monolith.notes: Crash containment comes from lease/fence checks, scoped capability sets, bounded retries and checkpoint resume; an engine-internal fault remains a whole-process (host) failure domain.

container_split.notes: OS boundaries contain module crashes better, but lease/fence authority must be re-proved across RPC and the shared audit store couples the containers anyway.

modular_monolith.notes: One process keeps one clock domain: deterministic WorkerAdapter + seeded fixed-rate schedule replays runs offline (S1-002 seed 20260824).

container_split.notes: Every RPC hop and separate scheduler adds nondeterminism the simulation interface must abstract away again; a simulation mode is in-process anyway.

modular_monolith.notes: Single writer and same-host file access hold by construction; measured p99 7.39 ms at 100 events/s leaves headroom.

container_split.notes: N containers contend for the single WAL writer on one host; multi-host split of a live WAL database is unsupported and a documented corruption risk.

modular_monolith.notes: One deployable unit; recovery is resume-from-latest-consistent-checkpoint; one set of logs, one audit anchor.

container_split.notes: N images plus orchestration, service discovery and coordinated recovery; every recovery path now spans a process boundary.

modular_monolith.notes: One runtime to monitor, upgrade and debug; hard module contracts give most of the maintainability benefit without the network.

container_split.notes: Distributed debugging, versioned RPC contracts, partial-failure handling and per-container observability are new permanent operating costs.

modular_monolith.notes: One process shares CPU/memory; measured headroom at MVP rates is ample (busy ratio <= 0.323 at 100 events/s), so the constraint is not binding yet.

container_split.notes: Per-module scaling and resource caps are the genuine gain; the shared single-writer SQLite store caps the benefit for the record path.

failure_scenarios.name: worker crash mid-run
failure_scenarios.detection: lease expiry with no heartbeat/progress and a missing or stale checkpoint
failure_scenarios.modular_monolith_recovery: engine marks the run FAILED(recoverable) and resumes from the latest consistent sha-verified checkpoint into a new Run with immutable lineage; bounded retry budget applies
failure_scenarios.container_split_recovery: same state machine only if the engine retains sole lease authority; a scheduler container reassigning leases independently weakens fencing and can double-execute

failure_scenarios.name: crash between transition and audit append
failure_scenarios.detection: open SQLite transaction rolls back; audit_anchor head and row count unchanged
failure_scenarios.modular_monolith_recovery: atomic rollback leaves state and audit consistent; a retried transition_key is a no-op returning the original event
failure_scenarios.container_split_recovery: an asynchronous or per-container audit writer can lose or fork audit rows across the crash; the hash chain and anchor diverge and invariant 8 is broken

failure_scenarios.name: policy/audit store unavailable or partitioned
failure_scenarios.detection: gateway op raises, or a mutating intent exists without a recorded outcome
failure_scenarios.modular_monolith_recovery: mutating ops return UNKNOWN_OUTCOME with reconciliation_required and are never blindly retried; reconcile() distinguishes RECONCILED_SUCCEEDED/FAILED and the gate blocks the latter
failure_scenarios.container_split_recovery: a split with per-container policy copies keeps serving stale policy during the partition (split-brain); detecting audit-mirror divergence across containers is not provided by the MVP

failure_scenarios.name: SQLite WAL writer contention
failure_scenarios.detection: write-latency growth and busy timeouts on the record path
failure_scenarios.modular_monolith_recovery: single in-process writer serializes by construction; measured baseline holds p99 <= 7.39 ms at 100 events/s
failure_scenarios.container_split_recovery: each added container multiplies writers contending for the one WAL writer; a multi-host split cannot share the live WAL file at all without replacing the storage engine

recommendation.failure_boundary: Worker crash is contained by lease/fence checks, bounded retries and checkpoint resume; an engine/journal fault is the host failure domain recovered by SQLite transactional rollback plus resume-from-checkpoint.
recommendation.deterministic_simulation_interface: WorkerAdapter protocol with the deterministic fake worker plus the seeded fixed-rate arrival schedule (S1-002 configuration.seed 20260824) gives replayable runs with no network or model access, in one process/clock domain.
assumptions: MVP event rates stay within the S1-002 measured envelope
workers are untrusted and all effects stay gateway-only
no hard multi-host or multi-runtime requirement exists today
migration_trigger: sustained measured demand approaches single-host capacity (S1-002 single-worker busy ratio at target rate is the leading indicator)
a hard requirement appears to run module runtimes on different hosts or with different runtime stacks
the audit store must leave SQLite, which requires a new formal trust-boundary review in the S1-003/S1-004 class
an organizational ownership split requires independent deployment cadence
non_goals: no production containers will be built from this research
no measured reliability claim from this design comparison
